run.question: Use the custom-crd runbook and check why custom CRD whale-watcher resources are not being reconciled by the operator in namespace app-96

report.summary: The requested custom-crd runbook does not exist for this target (fetch_skill returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND; the only runbook offered is service-troubleshooting, which covers connectivity, not CRD reconciliation), so the investigation was done directly against the cluster. The CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io exists and is healthy as an API object (group ocean.io, namespaced, kind WhaleWatcher, single version v1 served+storage, NamesAccepted/Established True), and the operator workload app-96/whale-operator is 1/1 ready with pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-75cl2 Running, Ready and 0 restarts (no crash, OOM, eviction or probe failures). What is demonstrably narrow is the operator's write authority: the only ClusterRole for ocean.io (ClusterRole whale-operator) grants just get/list/watch on whalewatchers, bound via ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator to the exactly-matching ServiceAccount app-96/whale-operator that the pod runs as, and there is no Role/RoleBinding in app-96 adding update/patch or status/events permissions. Independently, the CRD's v1 version declares no subresources block, so no status subresource is enabled even though the schema defines status.lastSeen/observationCount/phase. Two candidates therefore remain: a read-only RBAC grant that would reject any status update/patch the reconcile loop attempts (403 Forbidden), and a missing status subresource that would reject a /status write as not found even if RBAC allowed it. A third, unresolvable candidate is the operator's own code: /app/operator.py is mounted from Secret whale-operator, which cannot be read, and two log reads returned zero lines (status no_data), so no 403/ImportError/reconcile output exists to confirm which candidate actually fires. The WhaleWatcher custom resources themselves could not be read at all because kind whalewatchers is not one of the kinds the delivered Kubernetes tools enumerate, so the reported 'not reconciled' symptom is taken from the question, not verified in status/generation/conditions. No admission webhooks, ResourceQuotas, ConfigMaps with whale/ocean settings or additional whale-related workloads exist; the only cluster events in the window are the routine app-96 startup events of this operator. Conclusion is partial: the RBAC read-only grant and the missing status subresource are concrete, evidence-backed configuration gaps on the path a reconciler must write through, but the fault itself was not observed and the operator code/config is unreadable.

claims.text: CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io exists with spec.group ocean.io, scope Namespaced, names.kind WhaleWatcher, a single version v1 (served true, storage true), conversion strategy None, and conditions NamesAccepted=True (reason NoConflicts) and Established=True (reason InitialNamesAccepted).

The CRD's v1 version entry contains name, schema, served and storage but no subresources block, so the WhaleWatcher status subresource is not declared; the schema nonetheless defines status fields lastSeen, observationCount and phase.

Deployment app-96/whale-operator is 1/1 ready (readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, generation 1 = observedGeneration 1, conditions Available/MinimumReplicasAvailable True and Progressing/NewReplicaSetAvailable True); its container 'operator' runs image python:3.9-slim with command ["python","/app/operator.py"], env OPERATOR_NAMESPACE from fieldRef metadata.namespace, serviceAccountName whale-operator, and mounts volume operator-code from a Secret.

Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-75cl2 (namespace app-96) is owned by ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66, which is owned by Deployment whale-operator; the pod is phase Running, Ready=True, container 'operator' ready and started, restartCount 0, lastState empty, startedAt 2026-11-23T16:52:26Z, and it runs as ServiceAccount whale-operator.

The only ClusterRole rule set referencing ocean.io is ClusterRole 'whale-operator': apiGroups ["ocean.io"], resources ["whalewatchers"], verbs ["get","list","watch"] — no update, patch, create or delete, no whalewatchers/status resource, and no events permission.

ClusterRoleBinding 'whale-operator' binds ClusterRole 'whale-operator' to ServiceAccount 'whale-operator' in namespace app-96 — the same name and namespace recorded as the operator pod's spec.serviceAccountName, and ServiceAccount app-96/whale-operator exists.
Namespace app-96 contains no Role and no RoleBinding, so no namespace-scoped grant adds write verbs on whalewatchers or whalewatchers/status beyond the ClusterRole's get/list/watch.

All 6 cluster events in the authorized window are Normal events in app-96 describing the operator's own rollout: Deployment/ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet/SuccessfulCreate, Pod/Created, Pod/Scheduled, Pod/Pulled, Pod/Started (one each). No Forbidden, FailedCreate, Unhealthy, Evicted, OOMKilling or WhaleWatcher-related event was recorded.

No ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and no MutatingWebhookConfiguration exists in the cluster (both lists empty), and namespace app-96 has no ResourceQuota, so neither admission nor quota is intercepting WhaleWatcher writes or operator-created resources.
app-96 holds a single ConfigMap (kube-root-ca.crt) and no Service; across the cluster no ConfigMap name matches whale/ocean, so there is no ConfigMap-held operator or fault-injection setting to read.

app-96/whale-operator is the only whale/ocean-related deployment in the cluster (25 deployments total) and all 33 pods in the cluster are Running with ready containers and restartCount 0, so no sibling controller or restarted operator pod exists.

Leading candidate: the operator's ServiceAccount can only read WhaleWatchers (ClusterRole whale-operator verbs get/list/watch, no whalewatchers/status update/patch, no events create, no namespaced Role adding them), so any reconcile that writes status or patches the object would be rejected by the API server as Forbidden (HTTP 403) and the custom resource would stay unreconciled. This is a hypothesis because no 403 line, audit record or CR status was observable.

Second candidate: the WhaleWatcher CRD declares no subresources for v1, so a reconciler that writes through the status subresource (PUT/PATCH /apis/ocean.io/v1/namespaces/app-96/whalewatchers/<name>/status) would be rejected as not found even with write RBAC; status.phase/observationCount/lastSeen could then never be set.

Third candidate: the reconcile logic itself cannot be inspected because /app/operator.py is supplied by Secret 'whale-operator' (unreadable), so a bug such as a wrong apiVersion/group or hardcoded namespace, a missing Kubernetes client in python:3.9-slim, or a watch loop that never writes remains an unexcluded cause of non-reconciliation.

A crash/restart or resource-pressure explanation is contradicted: the operator pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, empty lastState, no OOMKilled/Evicted/BackOff/Unhealthy event, and no ResourceQuota restricts app-96.

A CRD-not-served or RBAC-subject-mismatch explanation is contradicted: the CRD reports Established/NamesAccepted True with v1 served and storage, and the ClusterRoleBinding subject (ServiceAccount whale-operator, namespace app-96) matches the pod's spec.serviceAccountName and existing ServiceAccount exactly.
Rejected: the operator is down, not ready or crash-looping. The deployment reports 1/1 available and the pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-75cl2 is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and no failure events.
Rejected: an admission webhook blocks WhaleWatcher writes. No ValidatingWebhookConfiguration or MutatingWebhookConfiguration exists in the cluster.

Verify and, if the reconciler writes status, extend the operator's authority (ClusterRole whale-operator or an added Role) with update/patch on whalewatchers and whalewatchers/status and create on events, or confirm the operator only needs read verbs; also add subresources.status to CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io if status-subresource writes are intended.

Obtain what this Run could not read: the contents of Secret whale-operator (operator.py and any hardcoded group/namespace), the WhaleWatcher objects' metadata.generation, .status and conditions in app-96, and the operator container's stderr on a reconcile attempt — these decide between the RBAC, status-subresource and code candidates.

gaps: The requested custom-crd runbook is not available: fetch_skill for 'custom-crd' returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND and named 'service-troubleshooting' as the only runbook of this target, so no CRD-specific runbook steps could be followed.

The WhaleWatcher custom resources themselves could not be read: kind 'whalewatchers' is not one of the kinds the delivered Kubernetes tools enumerate (the query was refused with INVALID_PARAMS), so their generation vs observed status, .status fields, finalizers and conditions — i.e. the actual evidence that reconciliation is not happening — are unverified.

Operator application output is missing: two fetch_pod_logs reads of whale-operator-5f695b7c66-75cl2 (default 1h window and explicit 2026-11-23T16:52:20Z–16:53:03Z, limit 200/100, no filter) returned zero lines with status no_data, so no Forbidden/ImportError/reconcile message could be read; no 'previous' container instance exists (empty lastState, restartCount 0).
Secret 'whale-operator' (source of /app/operator.py) cannot be read, so the operator's actual logic, apiVersion/group, target namespace and dependencies are unknown.

Prometheus was unavailable during this Run: get_metric_names for {__name__=~'.*whale.*|.*operator.*|.*ocean.*'} and an instant query for kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace="app-96"} both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no metric corroboration of operator activity exists.
The change_history integration is not configured, so when the ClusterRole/CRD configuration reached its current state cannot be established.

All object states are as of the queries at 2026-11-23T16:53–16:54Z; the namespace app-96, CRD, deployment and pod were all created at 2026-11-23T16:52:25–26Z, roughly 40 s earlier, so the month-long authorized window contains no earlier cluster state and the duration of non-reconciliation is unknown.
Whether the CRs were created before or after the operator started (i.e. whether an initial LIST should already have reconciled them) cannot be determined without reading the WhaleWatcher objects.
next_steps: Read the WhaleWatcher objects in app-96 (generation, .status.phase/observationCount/lastSeen, conditions, managedFields) with a client that can access ocean.io/v1 to confirm non-reconciliation and see how far the last write got.

Read the operator's stdout/stderr on a live reconcile attempt (or run the same Secret-mounted operator.py against a read-only token) to capture the exact 403 Forbidden vs 404 NotFound vs application error.
Inspect Secret whale-operator to confirm which file the container mounts as /app/operator.py and which apiVersion/group/namespace it uses.
Compare the intended reconciler contract with the ClusterRole whale-operator (get/list/watch only) and the CRD's missing subresources.status, and align them.
If status-subresource writes are intended, add subresources: {status: {}} to CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io and grant update/patch on whalewatchers/status (plus events create if events are emitted).

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
